summary: Inventory web applications run persistently on node2 and node3 port 8080. Node1 persistently load-balances port 80 across both backends. Round-robin, backend failover, remote access, and restart persistence were verified while retaining kernel 2.6.22-14-generic.
actions_performed: Created a Python 2.5-compatible inventory application on node2 and node3.
Configured SysV init startup for both backend services.
Created a Python 2.5-compatible round-robin reverse proxy on node1 with automatic retry of the alternate backend.
Configured SysV init startup for the load balancer.
Verified alternating traffic and single-backend failover.
Safely restarted node2, node3, and node1 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and service recovery.

evidence.summary: Node2 listens on port 8080 and returns HTTP 200 with complete inventory data, including after restart.
Node3 listens on port 8080 and returns HTTP 200 with complete inventory data, including after restart.

evidence.requirement: Node1 load-balances incoming HTTP on port 80
evidence.summary: Node1 listens on port 80. Four local and four cross-node requests alternated node2/node3 and returned HTTP 200 with load-balancer identity headers.
While node2 was stopped, node1 returned HTTP 200 through node3 for every request; node2 was then restored with its inventory intact.
Healthy baseline boot ID 398a8614… was captured, restart acknowledged, new boot ID effb9ce0… observed, and the port-8080 service and inventory data recovered.
Healthy baseline boot ID cbc3431f… was captured, restart acknowledged, new boot ID 8a3098ca… observed, and the port-8080 service and inventory data recovered.
Healthy baseline boot ID 1232f444… was captured, restart acknowledged, new boot ID dd2cac63… observed, and the port-80 load balancer recovered with both backends serving intact inventory data.
All nodes reported kernel 2.6.22-14-generic before and after their restarts.
